review_notes: Read the whole file and the Iterate.lean lemmas it depends on (iterateFrobenius_add/succ/one/naturality). The only repeated nontrivial reasoning I found is the successor/additive pair (Iso definitions, their four projection lemmas, and the two `ext` proofs). The Grp/CommGrp definitions are parallel but are thin wrappers over existing mathlib API, so I did not report them. I did not run Lean. The proposed rewrite is a sketch and is untested; the `Fact` and `hS` hypotheses in the `n, 1` case are the same as in the file.

findings.problem: `iterateRelativeFrobenius_succ` is the `m = n, n = 1` case of `iterateRelativeFrobenius_add`. The two proofs repeat the same argument: ext on the pullback, then rewrite `F_X^{n+1}` as a composite of Frobenius iterates, and commute it past `π.fst` using `iterateFrobenius_naturality`/`frobenius_naturality`. Likewise `iterateFrobeniusTwistSuccIso` repeats the construction of `iterateFrobeniusTwistAddIso` (`pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso _ _ _ ≪≫ pullback.congrHom rfl (by rw [... iterateFrobenius_add, add_comm])`). It also repeats the same four `_hom_fst`/`_hom_snd` simp lemmas. Any change to the twist identifications has to be made in both places.
findings.proposed_change: Keep `iterateRelativeFrobenius_add` as the single place where the composition law is proved. Define `iterateFrobeniusTwistSuccIso π p hS n` as `pullback.congrHom rfl (iterateFrobenius_one hS) ≪≫ π.iterateFrobeniusTwistAddIso p hS n 1`. Its `_hom_fst`/`_hom_snd` lemmas then follow from the `Add` ones by `simp`. Prove `iterateRelativeFrobenius_succ` from `iterateRelativeFrobenius_add n 1` together with `iterateRelativeFrobenius_one` applied to the twist `pullback.snd π (S.iterateFrobenius p hS n)`. The `iterateRelativeFrobenius_one` statement for that twist is `F^1 ≫ (congrHom ..).hom = relativeFrobenius`. This leaves one `ext` argument about Frobenius naturality instead of two.
findings.benefit: The Frobenius-naturality computation appears once, and the successor case becomes a corollary of the additive law, so the twist identifications cannot drift apart. The reader sees `succ` as the `n, 1` case of `add`.
